content.text: I wrote this for anyone who works, builds, or spends a lot of time with me! I can be intense, direct, opinionated, and extremely systems-oriented. At my best, those traits make me a great collaborator; at their worst, I can be a lot 😅. This is my attempt to make it all explicit: how to get the best out of working with me, where I tend to get in my own way, and what you should expect from me in return. Definitely a living doc, so if your actual experience conflicts with anything here, please trust your experience and tell me so I can improve!
My personality tests say I’m extreme in almost every direction 😅.
I’m social, disciplined, comfortable with disagreement, hard to rattle
My strengths and blind spots are the same traits at different intensities.
Systems thinking can become rigidity; high standards can make me intimidating
I wake up at 3:45am and work weird hours.
I trust people who act with agency, own their results + tell me the truth.
I owe you the autonomy to do that
Write first; meet for debate, ambiguity, or something personal
Lead with your rec + the context I need + a deadline
I lose messages in a 100+ convo queue.
Please nudge me if I’m blocking you!
Direct feedback makes both me + the work better
I take my hobbies way too seriously:

I taught myself to code at 12, built the world's #1 homework planner, then worked on the Apple Vision Pro and early Apple Intelligence prototypes. My senior thesis on the technological singularity convinced me to dedicate my career to helping society adapt to AGI. When ChatGPT launched, a weekly gathering in my living room became The AI Collective, a global nonprofit with over a quarter-million members and hundreds of chapters. I serve as chairman and am returning to what energizes me most: building from zero with exceptional people. Outside work, I'm a bookworm, natural bodybuilder, personal-systems nerd, and occasionally write and speak.

To be a loving, inspiring leader who helps others self-actualize by creating environments of passion and purpose. To invest deeply in family, friendship, and enduring relationships. To think rationally and systemically, act with agency, and realize my potential through lifelong learning, broad exploration, deep mastery, and relentless ambition. To play the long game while still stopping to smell the roses. To value the experiential over the material and peak experiences over passive comfort. To live with strength, energy, and an appetite for challenge and adventure, sustained by exceptional physical, mental, and social health.
To build the tools and institutions that turn AGI into broadly shared human flourishing. To make a dent in the universe.
Very high Conscientiousness (108) & Extraversion (106); very low Agreeableness (61) & Neuroticism (38). As in, top 1-5% most extreme for all four 😅

title.text: My dominant themes are in the Influencing and Executing domains.

content.text: : I work hard and possess a great deal of stamina. I take immense satisfaction in being busy and productive. I love to complete tasks, and my accomplishments fulfill me. I have a strong inner drive — an innate source of intensity, energy and power that motivates me to work hard to get things done.

: I can organize, but also have a flexibility that complements this ability. I like to determine how all of the pieces and resources can be arranged for maximum productivity. I have a natural ability to coordinate people and resources for maximum effectiveness. My creative flexibility in complex situations leads to greater efficiency.
: I have a great desire to learn and want to continuously improve. The process of learning, rather than the outcome, excites me. I provide your teammates with a logical perspective on things.

: I measure my progress against the performance of others. I strive to win first place and revel in contests. I motivate yourself and others to a higher standard of performance. I can raise a group’s achievement level by creating a culture of winning and aspiring to be the best.

: I want to make a big impact. I am independent and prioritize projects based on how much influence they will have on your organization or people around me. I want to do important work and are determined to make a difference. I want others to respect me for my significant contribution and willingness to work hard to achieve success.
I am a mission-oriented systems-builder energized by ambitious goals and rational debate. I thrive on turning chaos into order and driving a team toward a clear, world-changing objective.
I view my (very) high disagreeableness as a feature of my commitment to my mission. I believe that intellectual honesty and rigorous debate are the fastest path to the best ideas.

My Blind Spots (Where I Need Your Help)

I'm working to notice and correct these before they affect others. You are always invited (but never responsible) to flag them! If you name it, I will do my best to pause, understand the impact, and repair rather than defend it.

title.text: I LOVE systems and process. But sometimes situations call for fluidity, improvisation, or just vibing – and I can be too rigid when looseness would serve better.

title.text: My default is to do it myself, especially on things I used to own. This makes me a bottleneck.

content.text: Help me: Proactively own your domain. If I'm creeping into your weeds, say:
"Chappy, I've got this. Let me come back with a finished product."
I’ll recognize it as gift, not a challenge.

title.text: I have a high internal clock + can be overwhelming → I inadvertently judge or blame others for not keeping up.

content.text: Help me: Tell me if my pace is unsustainable for you. High performance AND psychological safety aren't opposites.

title.text: : When I'm underslept, dieting hard, overloaded, or frustrated, I can become tense, uncommunicative, abrasive, and harder to read.

content.text: If I land sharply, I should pause, reset, and repair rather than expecting you to deal with it.

title.text: I tend to pack my todo list beyond capacity, leaving no slack for serendipity, spontaneous connection, or the unexpected opportunities that often matter most.

content.text: Help me: If you see something worth my time, push for it.
I am effectively always working (usually 80-100 h/w 😅), but my core, most responsive hours are
. You can expect me to be highly engaged during this window. (

My mornings before 9am, as well as Tuesday and Thursday afternoons, are my protected deep work blocks (eg. coding, writing, researching, strategy). I will be slow to respond during these blocks. I work intensely on weekends, but I cherish this time for uninterrupted, creative deep work. Please respect this by avoiding non-urgent requests.
I believe meetings are for two things: 1) high-bandwidth debate to solve a hard problem, and 2) efficient, team-wide status updates and alignment.
I expect the meeting leader to arrive on time and with a clear (and ideally written) agenda.
I expect everyone on the call to be engaged and to contribute. The meeting leader is responsible for creating and facilitating these conditions.
A pre-read in advance before is a gift to everyone in the meeting –

if it’s more of a homework assignment rather than passive read! It's by no means required, but it is always appreciated and allows us to use our synchronous time for the highest-value and most informed discussions.
I am often juggling a very high volume (100+ of open lines. While I will see your message, it may occasionally take me
to respond to non-urgent pings. Please do not take this personally; it is a function of my batching system for managing focus. If you need a faster response, read on!

I believe the best work happens in long, uninterrupted blocks of focus. For any complex topic, my strong preference is to start with a written, well-structured document (like a Notion or Google Doc). This allows me to engage with your ideas deeply on my own schedule and it forces clarity of thought for everyone involved.

Be concise. Use bullet points. Get to the point quickly and put your rec or key question at the top. I trust you've done the deep thinking; you don't need to show all your work in the initial message. Minimal ChatGPT fluff please!
"does Chappy have all the context he needs to make an informed decision on this?"
If no, provide the necessary background docs / links. Reducing friction is the fastest way to get a response!
Whenever possible, our communications should happen in shared, public channels within the team.
This reduces redundant conversations, creates a shared context, and allows others to learn and contribute.
The Right Channel for the Job
Use the appropriate public Slack channel. If you need my specific input,
you must @ me or I will likely miss it
. I am in over 100 channels (in AIC) and rely on mentions to filter what's important.
To get my input on a document:
Share a Notion or Google Doc with me and
with a clear question and your recommendation. This ensures it hits my radar.
To pitch me a new, big idea:
Write a concise, one-page document outlining: 1) the problem, 2) the proposed solution, and 3) a concrete first step. Share this with me via Slack.
For an urgent, time-sensitive issue (≤ 3 hours):
Send me a text message prefixed with "URGENT:"
. This will get my immediate attention. My phone # is included in my email signature and on my Slack profile.
I am running a thousand miles an hour and am full of blind spots. Please help me see them! Your honest perspective is a gift that helps me and our shared mission get better.
Because I am constantly context-switching, the most effective way to give me feedback is to first get my attention. A simple Slack message like,
"Hey Chappy, do you have 10 minutes for some feedback on X later today?"
is the perfect way to start. This allows me to switch into the right mental frame to actually hear you.
Start with a neutral, specific observation. (eg.
"In the leadership sync yesterday, when we discussed the budget, I noticed we moved to a decision without hearing from the broader team."
Explain the impact this had on you or the project. (eg.
"The story I told myself was that we are prioritizing speed over rigor in our financial planning, which makes me concerned about future risks."
Open the door for a real conversation. (eg.
"I was hoping you could help me understand your thinking there?"

I aim to care personally while challenging directly. I intend to address the work or behavior rather than the person, but intent doesn't determine impact. If I land badly or make an unfair inference, tell me!
I believe that recognition is a critical part of a high-performance culture. My goal is to ensure you feel seen and valued for your contributions.

I frequently give public praise for specific, excellent work, especially in our Slack channels or team meetings. My style is often succinct and direct, but it is a sincere acknowledgment of a job well done.

The single greatest way I show my respect for your work is by giving you more of it. When you consistently deliver with excellence, I will respond by giving you more ownership, more freedom, and bigger, more interesting problems to solve.

I will champion you and your work in the rooms you are not in. I will use my network and my platform to create opportunities for you and to ensure your contributions are recognized by the people who matter.

I am a bibliomaniac. I read 50-100 books a year, and much of my personal and professional philosophy is a synthesis of frameworks from thinkers I deeply respect. If you want to understand the "why" behind how I operate, these books are the source material!
Read my full compendium of book notes here:
: The bible and foundational operating system for a principled and effective life.
: The essential guide to understanding our own cognitive biases and making better, more rational decisions.
: The tactical operating system for building the small, consistent habits that lead to remarkable results.
: How to build and maintain the strong personal and professional relationships that are the foundation of a happy and impactful life.
: The intellectual justification for my "paradoxical passions" and my belief in the power of being a T-shaped, cross-disciplinary thinker.
: A data-driven guide (my favorite) to what actually leads to a successful and meaningful life, challenging many common assumptions.
: The definitive diagnosis of the problem we are trying to solve: the collapse of community and social capital in the modern world. This is the "why" behind our in-person focus.
: Provides the core principles for building a community with a strong identity, clear boundaries, and meaningful rituals.
: A powerful philosophical argument that the key to a thriving society is structuring belonging and citizen-led action, which is the heart of the AIC's grassroots model.
: Our tactical bible for event design. It's why we obsess over having a clear purpose for every single event we host, from a small dinner to a large festival.
: A masterclass in simple, repeatable, and high-energy event formats. It's the "how-to" guide for much of what our chapters do.
: My primary playbook for architecting a culture of psychological safety, shared vulnerability, and purpose. All of the leaders around me have also read this book.
: The non-negotiable framework for how we give feedback. It's about caring personally while challenging directly.
: The user manual for how to receive feedback – even when it's poorly delivered – as a gift for personal growth.
: The tactical guide for navigating the high-stakes, emotionally charged conversations that are inevitable when doing ambitious work.
: These are the foundational texts that ignited my obsession and defined the core mission of The AI Collective.
: The definitive guide to thinking from first principles and building something truly new in the world.
: The core of how I think about inspiring a movement – it's not about what we do, but
: This book shapes our long-term strategy. We are building a resilient organization with a just cause, designed to last for generations.
